Sunrise City.description: Neon Echo's flagship pop track built around a euphoric morning-drive feeling. With valence at 0.84 and energy at 0.82, it sits at the bright, danceable end of the pop spectrum. The 118 BPM tempo keeps it moving without crossing into exhausting territory.
Sunrise City.decade_context: 2010s production — layered synths and a prominent vocal hook that defines the era's pop sound.

Midnight Coding.description: LoRoom's chill study companion. Instrumentalness of 0.82 means nearly no vocals, making it ideal when lyrics would break concentration. Energy at 0.42 is higher than Library Rain but still firmly in the lofi comfort zone.
Midnight Coding.decade_context: 2020s lofi revival — crisp but warm production referencing vinyl-era jazz.

Storm Runner.description: Voltline's rock anthem designed for physical effort and intensity. Energy 0.91 and 152 BPM place it among the fastest tracks in the catalog. Acousticness of 0.10 confirms full electric production with no acoustic softening.
Storm Runner.decade_context: 2000s rock production — distorted guitars, tight drums, no electronic padding.

Library Rain.description: The most acoustic and instrumental track in the lofi section. Acousticness of 0.86 and instrumentalness of 0.88 create a near-silent, vinyl-textured atmosphere. The 72 BPM tempo is the slowest in the lofi catalog, perfect for deep focus or winding down.
Library Rain.decade_context: 2010s lo-fi aesthetic — deliberate warmth and imperfection that evokes analog recording.

Gym Hero.description: Max Pulse's highest-energy pop track. At 0.93 energy and 0.88 danceability, it is built to sustain physical effort. Lyric density of 0.73 means it has more vocal content than typical workout tracks, adding a motivational layer.
Gym Hero.decade_context: 2010s pop production — punchy, compressed, radio-ready sound built for volume.

Spacewalk Thoughts.description: The most purely ambient track in the catalog. Instrumentalness of 0.97 and energy of 0.28 create a near-silence that dissolves into texture. The 1970s release decade reflects its roots in early synthesizer experimentation.
standout_features: very high acousticness (0.92) for an ambient track
Spacewalk Thoughts.decade_context: 1970s experimental ambient — long, evolving textures without conventional melody or rhythm.

Coffee Shop Stories.description: The only jazz track in the catalog. Instrumentalness of 0.74 preserves the improvisational feel of a live session. The 1960s decade places it in the classic cool-jazz era — warm, unhurried, and sophisticated.
standout_features: very high acousticness (0.89) — acoustic instruments throughout
Coffee Shop Stories.decade_context: 1960s cool jazz — subtle swing, conversational pacing, no electronic instrumentation.

Night Drive Loop.description: Neon Echo's darker, synthwave side. The 1980s production evokes late-night highway driving. Instrumentalness of 0.46 means it has some vocals but they are processed and atmospheric rather than lyric-forward.
standout_features: moderate energy (0.75) — intense but not exhausting
Night Drive Loop.decade_context: 1980s synth aesthetic — analog warmth, minor-key progressions, and neon-lit melancholy.

Focus Flow.description: LoRoom's explicitly focus-optimized track. At 0.40 energy and 80 BPM, it is slightly more present than Library Rain without crossing into distraction. Instrumentalness of 0.80 keeps vocals out of the way.
Focus Flow.decade_context: 2020s lo-fi — modern production techniques applied to a deliberately retro aesthetic.

Rooftop Lights.description: The indie pop outlier: high valence (0.81) and strong danceability (0.82) but from an indie perspective rather than mainstream pop. Energy at 0.76 is high without the aggression of Gym Hero. The uplifting mood tag sets it apart from typical indie introspection.
standout_features: strong danceability (0.82) for an indie track
Rooftop Lights.decade_context: 2010s indie pop — live-instrument warmth with some electronic layering.

Neon Sprint.description: The highest-danceability track in the catalog at 0.91 and near-maximum energy at 0.95. City Static's EDM production is built exclusively for movement and peak-energy environments. Minimal acousticness (0.03) confirms full electronic production.
Neon Sprint.decade_context: 2020s EDM — maximalist production with dynamics engineered around the drop moment.

Porchlight Letters.description: The catalog's folk anchor. Acousticness of 0.93 and energy of 0.31 capture the intimate porch-session feeling. Lyric density of 0.55 means it has more lyrical content than most acoustic tracks — storytelling is central to its identity.
Porchlight Letters.decade_context: 1990s American folk revival — acoustic guitar, close-mic vocals, minimal studio treatment.

Velvet Afterglow.description: Blue Meridian's R&B slow-burn. At 0.58 energy and 0.72 valence, it occupies a warm middle ground — neither passive nor energetic. The sensual mood tag and 2000s production place it in the neo-soul tradition.
standout_features: warm mid-energy (0.58) — groovy without being demanding
high danceability for its energy level (0.77)
Velvet Afterglow.decade_context: 2000s R&B — rich layering, smooth vocal production, and a groove-forward rhythm section.

Iron Horizon.description: The most intense track in the catalog. Energy 0.97, 168 BPM, and instrumentalness of 0.00 mean vocals are present and aggressive throughout. The 1990s decade places it in the heavy metal era of maximum amplification.
standout_features: fully vocal — lyrics are central, not atmospheric
Iron Horizon.decade_context: 1990s heavy metal — uncompressed loudness, distorted power chords, aggressive vocal delivery.

Golden Hour Drive.description: Sierra Vale's nostalgic country track. The 1970s decade reflects classic country before the pop crossover era. Moderate energy (0.52) and high valence (0.76) create the warm, wistful feeling of a long sunset drive on an empty road.
standout_features: 1970s classic country production — pedal steel, warm acoustic
moderate acousticness (0.57) — mix of acoustic and electric
Golden Hour Drive.decade_context: 1970s outlaw country — storytelling lyrics, organic production, and emotional directness.

Mirrorball Fever.description: Luna Ray's disco peak. Highest valence in the catalog at 0.90 and very high danceability (0.89). The 1970s decade anchors it in the original four-on-the-floor era. Liveliness of 0.81 is the highest in the catalog, suggesting a performance-event atmosphere.
standout_features: highest liveliness in catalog (0.81) — peak performance energy
1970s disco production — strings, brass, and driving bass
Mirrorball Fever.decade_context: 1970s disco — orchestral arrangements over a relentless four-on-the-floor beat.

Night Market Pulse.description: Solar Tide's hip hop entry. Lyric density of 0.88 is the highest in the catalog — this track is lyric-forward in the hip hop tradition. Danceability of 0.84 and energy of 0.69 balance movement with a controlled, deliberate groove.
standout_features: highest lyric density in catalog (0.88) — dense wordplay
2010s hip hop production — crisp 808 kicks, punchy hi-hats
Night Market Pulse.decade_context: 2010s hip hop — clean digital production with emphasis on lyrical delivery and rhythmic precision.

Quiet Constellations.description: The most peaceful and sparse track in the entire catalog. Energy of 0.18 and instrumentalness of 0.99 create near-silence — Aria Vale's classical composition has essentially no vocals and the slowest tempo (58 BPM). The 1900s decade reflects its roots in pre-recording-era classical tradition.
standout_features: slowest tempo (58 BPM) — unhurried to the point of stillness
Quiet Constellations.decade_context: Early 20th century classical — acoustic instruments only, no amplification, performance-hall dynamics.
